concept.name: Golden cross
concept.definition: A bullish moving-average crossover — classically the 50-day SMA crossing above the 200-day SMA — interpreted by technicians as confirmation of a long-term uptrend. It is a widely watched analytical convention, not a proven predictive law.
concept.intuition: The market's medium-term average climbing above its long-term average suggests that upward momentum has been sustained long enough to matter.
concept.mechanics: Identified on daily charts when the shorter (typically 50-day) moving average crosses up through the longer (typically 200-day) one; because both averages lag, the cross usually prints well after the actual low.
concept.failure_modes: Late by construction and whipsaw-prone in range-bound markets; by the time a golden cross prints, much of the advance has often already occurred.
concept.misconceptions: It is not a guaranteed buy signal or a law of markets — it records that an advance has been large and persistent; any forward-looking edge is an empirical question, not a property of the construction.
concept.example: MACD(50,200,1) turning positive marks the same 50/200 EMA golden cross in oscillator form.

citations.source: Moving Averages - Simple and Exponential | ChartSchool | StockCharts.com
